subject: Healthscope - model fit & safety follow-up and evals
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zheng <claire.zheng@healthscope.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-24T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (model fit + safety evals)

Hi Claire,

Thanks again for the time today - great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Goal: validate model fit for Healthscope's patient triage assistant (sensitive medical domain) and confirm safety/refusal behavior for high-risk prompts.
- Recommended baseline models to evaluate: redwood-alpha-2.7b (fast, quantized), redwood-beta-13b-qa (higher accuracy for long context), and an instruction-tuned open-13b variant for benchmark comparisons.
- Deliverables we will share by end of day tomorrow: initial eval CSV with accuracy/ROUGE-ish metrics, the safety prompt set (refusal/guardrail cases), and a short notes doc with recommended model/config (batching, kv cache settings).

Immediate asks for you:
1) Share any existing prompt sets or examples where the model should refuse or escalate to a human.
2) Confirm whether PHI will be sent to our hosted environment or if you require Private deployment (VPC/on-prem).

I've attached the preliminary eval template and the safety prompts we'll use as a starting point. Rishi is copied to help with SLA/throughput questions; Dev will jump in on the security/KMS details once we hear back about PHI.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: recommended_models_summary.pdf (summary), safety_prompt_set_v2.md (testing prompts)
From: Claire Zheng <claire.zheng@healthscope.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Barrett <tom.barrett@healthscope.com>, Healthscope Security Team <security@healthscope.com>
Date: 2026-03-24T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (model fit + safety evals)

Marissa - thanks for the recap and quick turnaround. A few notes from our side: 

- We attached a small set of real examples (anonymized) from support transcripts that represent the typical triage flows. See attached: healthscope_examples_redacted.csv.
- PHI: yes, some user messages will contain PHI. We need to understand Private deployment options and KMS integration before we can route live traffic.
- For the evals: can you include a specific metric for refusal correctness (false-accept vs false-refuse) and a per-prompt confidence score? Also want to understand how the model behaves on chained prompts (multi-turn escalation).

Can you confirm timeline for the deliverables? Ideally we want an initial report by EOD tomorrow to feed into our security review meeting Friday.

Thanks,
Claire
Product Lead - Conversational AI
Healthscope

Attachment: healthscope_examples_redacted.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zheng <claire.zheng@healthscope.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-24T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (model fit + safety evals)

Claire - perfect, thanks for sending the examples. Quick answers inline and next steps: 

- Timeline: we will run the initial model fits tonight and deliver the CSV with accuracy/refusal metrics + per-prompt confidence by tomorrow 17:00 PT. If anything shifts we will update you.
- Metrics: we will include refusal-precision, refusal-recall (to capture false-accept/false-refuse), overall intent F1, and a calibrated confidence score per prompt. We'll also include per-turn trailing context tests for multi-turn escalation.
- Private deployment: Dev will follow up on KMS/HSM and on-prem packaging. Short answer: we can support VPC with customer-managed KMS; details below.

Recommendation summary (short):
- Start with redwood-beta-13b-qa for quality-focused evals. If latency/cost become constraining, compare to redwood-alpha-2.7b quantized with our recommended prompt-engineering (explicit refusal templates + minimum context).
- Safety approach: 1) classifier + model-level refusal templates, 2) high-precision escape hatch (explicit regex / entity detectors) for PHI categories, 3) human-in-the-loop escalation for borderline cases.

Next steps (internal owners):
- Marissa: deliver initial eval CSV + summary (tomorrow EOD).
- Rishi: prepare throughput/cost estimate for running 100k requests/day on Dedicated vs Hosted (due Mon).
- Dev: draft KMS/VPC integration notes + checklist for Private (due tomorrow).
- Neha: prepare short regression checklist for model updates (prompt sets, eval harness).

I'll send the report as soon as the runs complete.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments (to follow): healthscope_eval_results_v1.csv, safety_prompt_set_v2.md
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zheng <claire.zheng@healthscope.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Healthscope Security Team <security@healthscope.com>
Date: 2026-03-25T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (model fit + safety evals)

Hi Claire and team - Dev from Redwood infra here. Quick note on Private/KMS options: 

- We support customer-managed KMS keys in both our VPC deployment and on-prem package. Key points: we never persist plaintext keys in our control plane; HSM-backed KMS can be used for additional compliance.
- Network: VPC peering + restricted egress can be configured; manifest required for IP whitelisting.
- Audit logs: we can enable token-level tracing with retention options (30/90/365 days) depending on your compliance needs.

Action items for your security team: please send a list of required compliance artifacts (SOC 2 scope, retention requirements, allowed regions). Once we have that, we can provide a Private deployment checklist and an estimated onboarding timeline (typically 4-8 weeks depending on infra approvals).

Regards,
Dev Patel
Director, Infra Security
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zheng <claire.zheng@healthscope.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-25T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (model fit + safety evals)

Claire - delivered the initial evals (attached). Highlights: 

- redwood-beta-13b-qa: best overall accuracy and lowest false-accept for refusal tests (refusal-precision: 0.92, refusal-recall: 0.87).
- redwood-alpha-2.7b (quantized): much lower cost, slightly lower refusal precision (0.82) but acceptable latency for bursty traffic.
- Notable regression risk: instruction tuning in open-13b variants sometimes leads to over-verbosity on refusal prompts; we include prompt templates to mitigate.

Attachments included: healthscope_eval_results_v1.csv, safety_prompt_set_v2.md, recommended_models_summary.pdf.

Next ask: Claire, can you confirm whether Healthscope prefers we run a small closed pilot on Hosted (with PHI redaction and minimal retention) or go straight to Private? If Hosted pilot is acceptable, we can get a test endpoint up in 48 hours and throttle traffic to avoid data residency/regulatory issues.

Thanks and happy to hop back on a quick call after you review the CSV.

- Marissa

Attachment stubs: healthscope_eval_results_v1.csv (results), safety_prompt_set_v2.md (prompt list), recommended_models_summary.pdf (one-page)
